explain.title: Air pollutants
explain.body: Your textbook defines an air pollutant as: “Any substance (solid, liquid or gas) in the air which has adverse effect on human health and quality of life is called an air pollutant.” Remember that pollutants may be solids, liquids or gases.

explain.title: Concentration in ppm
explain.body: Your textbook says: “The concentration of a pollutant is expressed in parts per million (ppm). A concentration of one ppm means one part of pollutant per million part of solid, liquid or gas mixture in which the pollutant is formed.” In simple terms, ppm tells how much pollutant is present in a very large amount of mixture.

explain.title: Major sources and smog

explain.title: Harmful effects

Do not confuse the effects of carbon monoxide with those of carbon dioxide: CO is poisonous and interferes with oxygen transport; higher CO₂ levels increase global warming.

explain.title: What acid rain means
explain.body: When rain water has pH between 4.2 and 4.4, it is known as acid rain. Learn this range exactly for a definition or short-answer question.

explain.title: How acid rain forms
explain.body: Burning fossil fuels releases SO₂. In the atmosphere, SO₂ can be converted to SO₃, which reacts with water to form H₂SO₄. Nitrogen oxides also react with water: 2NO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → HNO₃(g) + HNO₂(g). The acids form droplets that can be carried far by wind before falling as rain, hail, snow or fog.

explain.title: Effects of acid rain
explain.body: Acid rain makes soil more acidic and washes away nutrients. It can damage plants and forests, make water too acidic for aquatic animals, and contribute to harm from toxic substances leached from soil. It also damages crops and human-made structures such as buildings, statues, automobiles and bridges.

explain.title: Reducing agricultural damage
explain.body: Farmers can monitor soil conditions and, when necessary, add crushed lime (CaO) to neutralize acid.

steps.why: This is the textbook definition, so begin by stating what the greenhouse effect means.
steps.text: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect.

steps.why: The explanation begins with the Sun’s short-wave radiation reaching Earth.
steps.text: The sun emits short wave radiation that passes through greenhouse gases to heat the surface of the Earth.

steps.why: Earth gives out long-wave radiation, and greenhouse gases absorb most of it.
steps.text: At night, the hot Earth's surface emits longwave radiation that is mostly absorbed by green house gases.

steps.why: Absorption slows the escape of heat, so Earth cools more slowly and warms overall.
steps.text: This process of absorption prevents the radiation to reach space, reducing the speed at which the Earth can cool off.

steps.why: Finish by stating the result of the process.
steps.text: This increases the temperature of the Earth and causes global warming.

explain.title: Why gas concentration matters

explain.title: Know the AQI and protect yourself

yourTurn.question: Q10.2. Why does AQI not rise in Pakistan in hot days of summer?
solution: On hot summer days, the ground heats the air above it.

explain.title: Air pollutants and their sources
explain.body: Air pollution includes harmful gases and particulate matter. Vehicles, industries, fuel burning and dust can add pollutants to the air. Carbon monoxide is poisonous, while fine particles can harm the respiratory system.

explain.title: Greenhouse effect and global warming
explain.body: Some gases, including carbon dioxide and methane, absorb outgoing heat. More of these gases can strengthen the greenhouse effect and cause global warming and climate change.

explain.title: Acid rain and smog
explain.body: Sulphur and nitrogen oxides can contribute to acid rain. Photochemical smog forms when nitrogen dioxide and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight.

explain.title: AQI and people at risk
explain.body: The air quality index indicates how polluted air is and communicates health risk. Children, aged people and people with existing health problems are especially vulnerable.

explain.title: Reducing environmental harm
explain.body: Cleaner energy, efficient vehicles, controlled industrial emissions, less waste, environmental education and effective rules can all help reduce pollution.

notes.title: Air Pollutants
notes.answer: Smog reduces the carbon dioxide absorbed during photosynthesis, so it inhibits plant growth.
notes.explanation: Air pollution is harmful material in the air. It can harm people, other living things and the environment. Pollutants include gases such as carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide, as well as particles such as dust and smoke.
notes.simple: Air pollution means harmful substances in the air. Some are gases; others are tiny particles. They can make people ill and harm plants and the environment.

notes.title: Acid Rain
notes.explanation: Acid rain forms when oxides of sulphur and nitrogen mix with moisture in the air. For example, SO₃ reacts with water to make H₂SO₄, while NO₂ reacts with water to make HNO₃ and HNO₂. Acid rain can harm soil, plants, aquatic life, human health, agriculture and human-made structures.
notes.simple: Acid rain is rain containing acids made from gases in the air. It can damage living things and structures.
steps: Burning fossil fuels releases SO₂ into the air.
SO₂ can be changed into SO₃ in the atmosphere.
SO₃ reacts with water to form H₂SO₄.
NO₂ reacts with water to form HNO₃ and HNO₂.
The acids can reach the ground in rain, hail, snow or fog.

notes.title: Global Warming (Greenhouse Effect)
notes.answer: A higher concentration of greenhouse gases absorbs more thermal radiation, causing a greater increase in global warming.
notes.explanation: Greenhouse gases let most incoming short-wave sunlight reach Earth’s surface. The warmed surface gives out long-wave radiation, which these gases absorb. This slows the loss of heat to space and raises Earth’s temperature. For example, more CO₂ in the atmosphere increases heat absorption; melting ice and rising sea levels are possible effects of warming.
notes.simple: Sunlight warms Earth. Earth gives off heat, but greenhouse gases trap some of that heat, so Earth warms further.
examples: Example: burning coal, oil and natural gas adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
Example: melting ice in Antarctica and Greenland adds water to the seas and contributes to rising sea levels.
steps: Sunlight passes through greenhouse gases and warms Earth’s surface.
The warmed surface gives out long-wave radiation.
Greenhouse gases absorb much of this radiation, so less heat escapes to space.
The temperature of Earth rises; this is global warming.
notes.checkQuestion: Why does a higher concentration of greenhouse gases increase global warming?
notes.checkAnswer: Greenhouse gases absorb some long-wave radiation from Earth and slow the escape of heat to space.

notes.title: Strategies to reduce environmental issues
notes.answer: A catalytic converter reduces harmful emissions from an automobile engine by changing them into less harmful substances.
notes.explanation: Environmental problems can be reduced by lowering pollution at its source and protecting people from polluted air. Planting trees, using catalytic converters, removing sulphur dioxide from flue gas and switching to renewable energy are important strategies. When air quality is poor, people—especially high-risk groups—should reduce outdoor exposure and follow safety advice.
notes.simple: Make less pollution, use cleaner energy, and avoid breathing polluted air.
examples: A catalytic converter changes harmful carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide.
Solar and wind energy can generate electricity without burning fossil fuels.
steps: Plant trees: they absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and trap some particulate matter on their surfaces.
Use catalytic converters: they change nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons into less harmful substances.
Reduce sulphur dioxide: use fuels with less sulphur or remove sulphur dioxide from flue gas using an adsorbent such as calcium oxide.
Use renewable resources such as sunlight, wind, water, geothermal energy and biomass.
When air quality is poor, limit outdoor activity, use a well-fitted N95 mask if going out, keep indoor air clean and seek medical advice for worrying symptoms.
notes.checkQuestion: Name one strategy that can reduce harmful emissions from automobiles.
notes.checkAnswer: Planting trees, using catalytic converters, reducing sulphur dioxide from flue gas and using renewable energy can help reduce environmental issues.

written.text: Explain greenhouse effect. How is global warming dangerous for us?
modelAnswer: The progressive warming up of the Earth's surface due to blanketing effect of man-made carbon dioxide, methane, water vapours and other gases in the atmosphere is called Greenhouse Effect.
The Sun emits short-wave radiation that passes through greenhouse gases and heats Earth’s surface.
At night, Earth’s surface emits long-wave radiation, which is mostly absorbed by greenhouse gases; this slows the escape of heat to space and raises Earth’s temperature.
Global warming can expand seawater and melt ice in Antarctica and Greenland, raising sea levels and threatening low-lying coastal areas.
It can also increase rainfall and floods, affect agriculture and food production, and make summers longer and hotter and winters shorter and warmer.

written.text: Q10.1. Major Pakistani cities experience a very high AQI in winter which renders them the most polluted cities in the world. Point out some of the major causes of high AQI in these cities.
modelAnswer: Vehicle exhaust and heavy traffic release gases and particulate matter.
Industries and power generation add further emissions.
Burning fuels, waste and crop residues can increase smoke and particles.
Construction activity and road dust add particulate matter.
In winter, stagnant air and temperature inversion can trap pollutants close to the ground, raising the AQI.

written.text: Q10.2. Why does AQI not rise in Pakistan in hot days of summer?
modelAnswer: On hot summer days, the ground heats the air above it.
The warm air rises and carries pollutants upward, where they disperse and mix with a larger volume of air.
Unlike winter conditions, pollution is less likely to remain trapped close to the ground.
Therefore, AQI may not rise as it does during winter pollution episodes.

written.text: Q10.3. How has climate change affected Pakistan during the last five years?
modelAnswer: In recent years, Pakistan has experienced severe heatwaves and unusually high temperatures.
Irregular and intense rainfall has contributed to damaging floods in some areas, while other areas face dry conditions and water shortages.
These events damage homes, roads and other infrastructure and affect people's health and livelihoods.
Agriculture and crops are also affected by heat, floods and changing water availability.
